entries.title: Set up your own email domain yourself
entries.summary: **Settings > Domains**, for the organization and for each event, walks you through the From address, the DNS records and verification, with clear statuses and errors. Copy the instructions for Slack or Teams, or email them to your IT contact straight from the page. Sessionboard checks the records every 10 minutes and emails you when they verify, and the organization's page lists every event's address and status.

enable.path: Ask support to enable Custom Sending Domain for the organization; then Settings → Domains → add your From address and the DNS records it shows

where.path: Org Settings → Domains; Event Settings → Domains

entries.use_case: Email from the customer's own domain is the #1 deliverability and trust fix, and it used to need support. Now the organizer or their IT contact does it, with Slack/Teams-ready instructions, auto-verification every 10 minutes and an org-wide status page.

cs_action.note: Gated by the org flag custom_sending_domain (Admin → Features & Enhancements). Turn it on for the customer, then point them at Settings → Domains. Staff skip the flag check, so a CSM can also run the setup for them.

internal.staff_path: Admin → org → Features & Enhancements → Custom Sending Domain; site domains stay staff-only on the same Domains page.
internal.when_to_bring_up: Deliverability complaints, onboarding, any customer not yet on a custom sending domain, SPF/DMARC questions from IT.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer still sending from a Sessionboard address; prioritise those with open deliverability tickets.
internal.gotchas: Per-event addresses are listed on the organization's page with their status. Every org that already had an org or event custom sender was switched on automatically at release, so check before asking support to enable it. The sender field in Admin settings is now read-only and links to Settings → Domains. Gmail, Outlook.com and other free-mail addresses are rejected, since only the provider can add DNS records.

entries.title: Evaluation plans: Replace cleans up the whole round
entries.summary: The **Replace not-yet-reviewed** and **Replace all** options now remove assignments on submissions that no longer match the rule and take those submissions out of the round, so the round count matches the filter; the preview and confirmation show how many submissions leave. Reviewed assignments are still kept with Replace not-yet-reviewed, and entered scores are never deleted.

where.path: Event → Evaluations → plan → Assignments → Assign reviewers → Replace not-yet-reviewed / Replace all

entries.use_case: Program chairs who re-track or re-categorise submissions after a round was assigned no longer end up with a round whose count disagrees with its filter, or with reviewers holding abstracts that moved out of their track.

cs_action.note: Replace all now removes assignments on submissions that fell out of the filter, including reviewed ones. Customers who use Replace all mid-round should read the confirmation counts; walk any medical/scientific customer through it before their next assignment pass.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says the round count does not match the filter, or reviewers still see submissions that were moved to another track.
internal.who_should_get_it: Everyone running round-based evaluations; especially multi-track scientific programs that correct categories after assignment.
internal.gotchas: Scores are never deleted even when an assignment is removed. Replace not-yet-reviewed keeps any assignment with review activity.

entries.title: Status filters include custom statuses
entries.summary: In evaluation plan filters and Automations, **Status is Pending** now also matches submissions in a custom status under Pending such as **In Review**, so an Assign reviewers automation no longer skips them with a filter mismatch.

where.path: Event → Automations → When card → Status filter; Evaluations → plan → submission filters

entries.use_case: Customers with custom statuses (In Review, Shortlisted…) under a standard one no longer need a filter per custom status, and automations stop silently skipping submissions that sit in one.

cs_action.note: Any customer whose Assign reviewers automation showed "filter mismatch" in Delivery history for sessions in a custom status: this is the fix. Tell them.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Delivery history shows skipped runs with "filter mismatch"; a customer asks why In Review sessions were not assigned.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using custom statuses together with Automations or evaluation plan filters.
internal.gotchas: To match a single custom status, pick that status in the filter instead of its parent.

entries.title: Automations: Contact created trigger
entries.summary: People automations can fire once for each new contact, narrowed by where they came from: added by your team, imported, from an integration, or from a form or portal.

enable.path: Event → Automations → New automation → People → When: Contact created → Created through

where.path: Event → Automations → When card

entries.use_case: Welcome emails and task creation the moment a speaker or contact lands on the event — and only for the sources you choose, so people who filled in their own details are not emailed twice.

cs_action.note: A good demo moment for any customer importing speaker lists or syncing from a registration platform.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Onboarding, "how do I welcome new speakers automatically", any customer doing imports or integrations into an event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer using Automations; especially those importing or syncing contacts.
internal.gotchas: Contacts created through the Public API, and contacts created at the organization level without an event, do not fire this trigger.

entries.title: Automations: email your team, and react only to the person's own changes
entries.summary: A Send email step can also email event team members and team tags, or only them. Field-change triggers gain **Only when the submitter makes the change** (sessions) and **Only when the contact makes the change** (people), so edits by your team, imports and integrations don't fire them.

enable.path: Event → Automations → Send email step → Team members; When card → Only when the submitter / contact makes the change

where.path: Event → Automations → Send email step and When card

entries.use_case: "Tell me when a speaker updates their own bio" is now one automation: it emails the team, and it ignores the team's own edits and imports so it does not fire on every bulk update.

cs_action.note: Customers who turned off a field-change automation because it fired on imports can turn it back on with the new checkbox.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks to be notified of speaker self-service edits, or complains an automation fires during imports.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer using Automations.
internal.gotchas: Each email needs at least one recipient. A team tag resolves when the email sends, so it reaches whoever holds the tag at that moment.

entries.title: Custom success page on Awards and Interest Forms
entries.summary: Write the message applicants and speakers read after they submit, in place of the default "What's next?" list.

enable.path: Awards → form builder → Success page tab; CRM → Interest Forms → form → Success page message

where.path: Awards form builder → Success page; Interest Form wizard → Details

entries.use_case: Awards and CRM customers can tell applicants exactly what happens next — when finalists are announced, what to prepare — instead of a generic list, which cuts the "what now?" emails after a submission.

cs_action.note: Available to anyone with Awards or Speaker CRM; nothing to enable beyond the add-on itself.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Awards program setup, Interest Form setup, any customer asking to change the confirmation text.
internal.who_should_get_it: Awards and Speaker CRM customers.
internal.gotchas: Leave the editor empty to keep the default list. Confirmation number, PDF download and Return to Portal still appear.

entries.title: Require secure links on URL fields
entries.summary: A URL field can save every `http://` link as `https://`, in the admin, submission forms and Awards applications.

enable.path: Settings → Fields → URL field → Require secure links (https://)

where.path: Org or Event Settings → Fields → a URL field

entries.use_case: Speaker websites and LinkedIn links pasted as http:// break on HTTPS-only program sites and embeds; this normalises them at save time with no cleanup pass.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Mixed-content warnings on a program site or embed; a customer cleaning up speaker URLs.
internal.who_should_get_it: Everyone publishing speaker or session links.
internal.gotchas: Off for new fields by default. Links already saved keep their address until someone edits them.

entries.title: Content galleries: My list goes home with the visitor
entries.summary: **Add to calendar** downloads saved sessions as a calendar file and **Email me my list** sends every saved item with its link. Recordings can be added to a gallery straight from the Media Hub with **Add to gallery**.

enable.path: Early Access → Preview → Content Galleries

where.path: Published gallery → My list; Marketing → Media library → recording → Add to gallery

entries.use_case: A visitor who saved sessions in a gallery can take the list to their calendar or inbox, which is the moment a content library turns into attendance and a captured email.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Content Galleries pilots; customers asking how a gallery drives registrations or captures leads.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers in the Content Galleries preview.
internal.gotchas: Add to calendar appears only once a saved item has a start time. Embargoed details stay hidden in the email; sending is rate-limited.

entries.title: Agenda embeds show any session field
entries.summary: The **Agenda** field tab lists every standard and custom session field, up to nine in the session pop-up.

enable.path: Embeds are enabled per event by support; then Event → Embeds → embed → Fields → Agenda tab

where.path: Event → Embeds → an agenda embed → Fields → Agenda

entries.use_case: Customers embedding the agenda on their own site can show CE credits, room, level or any custom field in the session pop-up without a feed and custom code.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks to show a custom field (credits, level, track colour) on their embedded agenda.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with Embeds enabled on an event.
internal.gotchas: Nine fields maximum in the pop-up; JSON and XML feeds are not limited. Ticking Starts At or Ends At also prints the time on the grid card.

entries.title: Evaluation plans: clearer assigning
entries.summary: The Assign button counts the evaluations it will create, **Done** on the Assignments step is now **Close without assigning**, and leaving with an unassigned change asks first. The same applies to Awards rounds.

where.path: Event → Evaluations → plan → Assignments step; Awards → round → Assign reviewers

entries.use_case: Chairs stopped losing assignment rules by clicking Done thinking it saved; the button now says what it does and the count makes the blast radius obvious before it is committed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports "my assignments disappeared" after configuring a rule.
internal.who_should_get_it: Everyone running evaluations or Awards rounds.

entries.title: Interest Forms: Speakers Only forms assign without a session
entries.summary: Assigning a Speakers Only submission adds its speakers to the event's contacts without creating a session.

where.path: CRM → Pipeline → submission → Assign to event

entries.use_case: Speakers Only forms are the CRM's general intake; assigning one to an event used to create an empty session the team then had to delete.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A CRM customer complains about empty sessions appearing after assigning interest-form submissions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Speaker CRM customers using Speakers Only forms.

entries.title: The Site Events page now shows on your public site
entries.summary: Turning on **Show Events page** in an organization Site now adds an **Events** tab to the public site, listing your upcoming or hand-picked events. Each event links to its own Site or an external page; events with no link show their name and date.

enable.path: Site → Pages → Events → Show Events page, then Publish

where.path: Organization Site → public site → Events tab; builder: Pages → Events

entries.use_case: Organizations running several events can give visitors one public list of them from their Site, with each event linking to its own Site or registration page.

cs_action.note: Customers who switched on the Events page and saw nothing publicly (the builder used to say it was not live yet): it now shows after Publish.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why the Events page is missing from their public Site, or wants one landing page for a portfolio of events.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations with an org-level Site and more than one event.
internal.gotchas: Only org-level Sites show the Events tab; event-level Sites never do. Filter mode leaves out template and sandbox events.

entries.title: Awards: match reviewers by category and add them from your reviewer pool
entries.summary: Tick **Match each submission to reviewers in its category** when assigning a round, and each entry goes only to the reviewers who judge its category, spread evenly. **Add from reviewer pool** adds several people who review in your other programs at once, and a **Review setup** card on the Assign tab shows the review window, uncovered categories and unassigned entries. Single assignments email the reviewer only while the round's review window is open.

where.path: Awards → program → round → Assign; Awards → program → Edit → Rounds step

entries.use_case: Programs with category panels no longer match hundreds of reviewers to categories by hand, can seat last year's judges in a couple of clicks, and stop emailing reviewers about assignments weeks before they can start reviewing.

cs_action.note: Good moment to show category matching to any Awards customer with category-tagged reviewers.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Awards customers setting up a review round, assigning reviewers by category by hand, or asking why reviewers got assignment emails before review opened.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every Awards customer, especially multi-category programs and returning programs with an existing judge pool.
internal.gotchas: Reviewers without a category are skipped when matching by category. Bulk adds do not re-invite people already in the program; use Resend Invite on the Reviewers tab. Invitations default to off in the pool dialog and in program setup. A round with no review dates counts as open for the assignment email. Nothing assigns new submissions automatically on arrival.

entries.title: Swapcard: push your tree structure from Sessionboard
entries.summary: Set a mapped tree field's **Tree owner** to **Owned by Sessionboard** and Sessionboard creates and updates the Swapcard tree before each sync. **Push tree now** previews every change before anything is sent, renames keep the Swapcard value, values still in use are hidden rather than deleted, and **Create in Swapcard** adds a missing tree field. Trees stay **Owned in Swapcard Studio** until an admin switches them.

enable.path: Org Settings → Integrations → Swapcard → Session or Speaker field mappings → Tree structure in Swapcard → Tree owner: Owned by Sessionboard

where.path: Org Settings → Integrations → Swapcard → field mappings → Tree structure in Swapcard

entries.use_case: Customers who maintain tracks and topics in Sessionboard no longer have to rebuild the same tree by hand in Swapcard Studio and keep the two in step every time a value changes.

cs_action.note: Switching a tree to Owned by Sessionboard lets Sessionboard edit the customer's Swapcard tree. Walk the customer through the preview dialog before their first push.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Swapcard customers whose tracks or topics drift between Sessionboard and Swapcard, or who ask why a renamed value broke in Swapcard.
internal.who_should_get_it: Swapcard customers who author their tree fields in Sessionboard.
internal.gotchas: Default stays Owned in Swapcard Studio, so nothing changes until someone opts in. Values added in Studio are never deleted, only hidden. Push is unavailable while field mappings have unsaved edits. Needs the Sync Integrations permission on the event. Pushing into an existing Swapcard tree with no values at all cannot place top-level values; recreate the field from the panel instead.

entries.title: Coordinator: Recent runs show progress and an accurate deferred count
entries.summary: A run in progress now reads **N of M speakers reached so far** and updates on its own, instead of showing every speaker as deferred. When a run finishes, **deferred** counts only speakers it never reached, and speakers the agent errored on show as **N failed**.

where.path: CRM → Coordinator → Dashboard → Recent runs

entries.use_case: Event teams watching a run no longer see a large amber 'speakers deferred' warning for the whole 30–40 minutes it takes, and the finished count now tells them who actually still needs a follow-up.

cs_action.note: Fix to an existing Coordinator surface; nothing to enable.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A Coordinator customer reports hundreds of deferred speakers on every run, or a deferred count while a run is still going.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every event with the Coordinator on.
internal.gotchas: Contacts assigned a form directly but not on the event (not a contact on the event and not in a session) are no longer picked up as eligible, so eligible counts can drop. Older runs keep the numbers they were recorded with.

entries.title: Team Lead summarizes Contacts, Applications, Send, Reports, Sponsors and Exhibitors
entries.summary: Open **Ask Team Lead** on the Contacts, Applications, Send campaigns, Reports, Sponsors or Exhibitors list and **What you have here** shows the page's counts, such as contacts by record type or campaigns by status, instead of saying it cannot summarize the page. The summaries are counts only, with no names, emails or message content.

where.path: Event → Contacts / Applications / Send / Reports / Sponsors / Exhibitors → Ask Team Lead

entries.use_case: Admins who ask Team Lead to walk them through these busy list pages get an answer grounded in their own event's numbers straight away.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says Team Lead replied "I can't summarise this page's settings yet" on one of these pages.
internal.who_should_get_it: Everyone using Team Lead.
internal.gotchas: The Advocacy campaign list and Brand pages still have no page summary.

entries.title: Public API: Awards programs, submissions and reviews
entries.summary: API tokens and OAuth apps can now be granted **read:awards** and **write:awards**, which open the public API's Awards routes for programs, categories, rounds, promo codes, submissions and reviews.

enable.path: Org Settings → API tokens → Create token → tick read:awards and/or write:awards

where.path: Org Settings → API tokens; OAuth consent screen

entries.use_case: Awards customers can sync programs and submissions with their own systems, such as an AMS or a data warehouse, instead of exporting spreadsheets.

cs_action.note: Point Awards customers with integration or reporting requests at the new scopes and the API reference.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Awards customers asking for an API, an AMS sync, or automated submission exports.
internal.who_should_get_it: Awards customers with a developer or integration partner.
internal.gotchas: No endpoint creates submissions or writes review scores; submissions are created through the portal. Deletes answer 409 until ?force=true when the program has submissions, the round has assignments, the promo code was redeemed or the category is in use. A token with no scopes can read Awards but not write.

entries.title: Bundled session campaigns confirm the number of emails
entries.summary: With **Bundle session participants onto one email** on, **Ready to send** and the confirm dialog now show the number of emails that will go out, matching **Sent** in the run history, instead of the number of people.

where.path: Send → Campaigns → campaign → Schedule → Ready to send / confirm

entries.use_case: Teams sending one email per session can trust the number they confirm, instead of seeing 23 recipients and wondering why only 2 emails went out.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports the confirm count did not match what a bundled session campaign sent.
internal.who_should_get_it: Everyone sending Sessions campaigns with bundling.
internal.gotchas: The count is emails only while bundling is on; turn it off and it goes back to people.

entries.title: File request uploads share one notification row
entries.summary: Repeat uploads to the same file request now update one unread row in the bell and the notifications inbox, with the latest upload and a running count, instead of adding a row per upload.

where.path: Header bell; Notifications inbox

entries.use_case: Admins on a busy file request see one line per request instead of a bell flooded with a row for every upload.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer complains the bell fills up with File Request Submitted rows.
internal.who_should_get_it: Everyone with File Request Submitted notifications on.
internal.gotchas: Once the row is read, the next upload starts a new row. Slack is not re-sent when a row is updated.

entries.title: Integrations tell you when a sync stops
entries.summary: When a sync keeps failing for a reason you can fix, the app's page shows a warning saying what is wrong and how many syncs have failed. The reasons covered are placeholder credentials, credentials the vendor rejected, and a linked event the vendor doesn't recognise. The warning clears after the next sync that succeeds.

where.path: Event → Apps → the app's page; Organization → Apps → the app's page

entries.use_case: A rejected API key or a deleted destination event used to fail quietly until someone read the sync log or a speaker noticed the agenda was stale. Now the customer sees the cause and the fix on the app's page the day it starts failing.

cs_action.note: Sync Doctor raises these from its open issues; Solutions sees the same issue in Sync Doctor and the #sync-doctor Slack channel. Only customer-fixable causes reach the banner; engineering causes go to Jira.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why their agenda or speakers stopped updating on the registration platform or app.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer with a connected program integration (Cvent, Swoogo, Bizzabo, Stova, Swapcard, ASP and the Apps Engine connectors).
internal.gotchas: If staff paused scheduled syncs, the banner says so, and a successful sync clears the banner but does not resume the schedule. Resume it from Sync Doctor.

entries.title: Archived fields leave column pickers and stay read-only
entries.summary: An archived field is no longer offered in the **Columns**, filter and sort pickers on the Contacts and Sessions lists. On a contact profile its stored value shows read-only with no inline editor, and Sessionboard refuses new values for it until you **Restore** the field.

where.path: CRM → Contacts and Program → Sessions → Columns; contact profile; Library → Fields / Event Settings → Fields → Archive

entries.use_case: Archiving a field now does what it promises: the field stops cluttering list columns and nobody can quietly overwrite the historical values it holds.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports an archived field still showing in the column picker, or someone editing a value on an archived field.
internal.who_should_get_it: Everyone who archives fields.
internal.gotchas: Org-wide archives apply in every event; event archives only in that event. A saved view that already had the archived column still loads. Bulk saves skip the archived field and save the rest; a single-field save is refused.

entries.title: Per-role Min/Max Participants columns on the Sessions grid
entries.summary: Each participant role now has **Min Participants: <Role>** and **Max Participants: <Role>** columns on the Sessions grid. Edit them in place or with **Bulk edit**; only that role's limit changes, and the role inventory cells update.

enable.path: Ask support to enable participant inventory; then Program → Program Settings → Agenda → Participant Inventory → Enable participant inventory, and add the columns from the Sessions grid's Columns picker

where.path: Program → Sessions → Columns → Min Participants: <Role> / Max Participants: <Role>

entries.use_case: Program teams can set "two to four speakers and one moderator" across the whole program from the grid in minutes, instead of opening every session.

cs_action.note: Columns are hidden until added from the Columns picker.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Customers using per-role limits who set them session by session.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with participant inventory on and Sessions 2.0 roles.
internal.gotchas: Role minimums that add up to more than the session's total maximum are rejected with an error. Field Rules cannot set per-role limits yet.

entries.title: Field Rules can set Min and Max Participants
entries.summary: An Assignment rule that sets **Min Participants** or **Max Participants** now writes the session's own participant limits, for example 2 to 6 whenever **Format** is Panel. A limit that doesn't fit the session is skipped without failing the save.

enable.path: Field Rules and participant inventory are turned on by support; then Library → Fields → Field Rules → Add Rule → Assignment

where.path: Library → Fields → Field Rules; Program → Sessions grid Min/Max Participants columns

entries.use_case: Teams that already know a panel needs 2–6 people and a talk needs 1 can let the format set the limits automatically instead of typing them on each session.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer built a Field Rule for Min/Max Participants and it had no effect (it used to write a value nothing read).
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using both Field Rules and participant inventory.
internal.gotchas: Total limits only; per-role targets need a design decision. Existing sessions pick it up only when the condition field is saved again.

entries.title: Advocacy: share to LINE and Instagram
entries.summary: Turn on **LINE** and **Instagram** under a campaign's **Share channels**. LINE opens LINE's share page with the tracked link and copies the post; Instagram copies the caption and hands the card to the phone's share sheet, or downloads it on a computer.

enable.path: Marketing → Advocacy → campaign → Edit campaign (or Quick Launch) → Share console → Share channels → LINE / Instagram

where.path: Advocacy campaign Share channels; the advocate's Creator console; Analytics → Channel mix

entries.use_case: Events with audiences in Japan, Taiwan and Thailand, or speakers who live on Instagram, can now give advocates a one-tap share where their followers actually are, still tracked back to each person.

cs_action.note: Off by default: new campaigns start with LinkedIn only and existing campaigns keep their saved channels, so the organizer has to turn LINE / Instagram on per campaign.

internal.when_to_bring_up: APAC customers, consumer-facing or creator-heavy events, anyone asking why Advocacy is LinkedIn-centric.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running Advocacy campaigns with APAC or Instagram-first speakers.
internal.gotchas: Instagram has no web share link: on desktop the card downloads and the caption is copied; links in captions are not clickable (link sticker or bio). LINE caches link previews, so a stale preview may show on a reused link. Closing the phone share sheet records no share.

entries.title: Domains tells you when your sending domain was never authenticated
entries.summary: For an address support set up before **Settings > Domains** existed, the organization's Domains page now says when the domain **has never been authenticated with SendGrid**, instead of reading "has not been checked yet" forever. A check SendGrid didn't answer now says it is retried every hour, rather than calling a fresh check too old to rely on.

where.path: Org Settings → Domains → Sending as …

entries.use_case: An organization whose mail was going out unsigned now sees it on the Domains page, with a clear next step, instead of a status that never resolves.

cs_action.note: Any org that now shows "has never been authenticated with SendGrid" is sending unsigned mail. Help them set the domain up under Settings → Domains (Change address, same address, add the DNS records).

internal.when_to_bring_up: Deliverability complaints from an org whose sending address was set up by support before self-serve Domains.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations on a custom sending address that predates Settings → Domains.
internal.gotchas: Only the legacy "Sending as" banner shows this line; addresses set up through Domains use the status badge. The never-authenticated message lists no failing records, because SendGrid has none for that domain. Updates after the hourly check runs.

enable.path: Ask support to enable Custom Sending Domain for the organization; then Settings → Domains

entries.title: File request uploads share one line in the daily summary
entries.summary: On the **Daily summary** email frequency, repeat **File Request Submitted** notifications now collapse into one line per file request with a count, such as *(3 submissions)*, instead of one line per upload.

where.path: Daily summary email

entries.use_case: Admins on the daily summary see one line per busy file request instead of a digest that lists every single upload.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer on the daily summary says it is flooded with File Request Submitted lines.
internal.who_should_get_it: Everyone with File Request Submitted email on the Daily summary.
internal.gotchas: Once a summary has gone out, the next upload starts a new line. At Immediately, each upload still sends its own email. The bell/inbox collapse shipped separately (file-request-uploads-share-one-notification-row).

entries.title: Visit: open questions no longer need an answer ID
entries.summary: Mapping a Sessionboard text field to a Visit free-text (open) question now fills in the question's answer ID for you, shown as **· assigned automatically**, with no ID to paste. The text syncs even on a run where Sessionboard couldn't load the expo's question list, instead of failing with "Answer not found".

where.path: Apps → Visit → Map Speaker Fields

entries.use_case: Mapping job titles or other free text onto Visit questions is a pick from a list, with no hunting for answer IDs, and the text arrives in Visit as typed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A Visit customer asks where to find the answer ID for an open question, or sees "Answer not found" on text answers.
internal.who_should_get_it: Visit customers mapping text fields onto expo questions.
internal.gotchas: Rows mapped before this keep any pasted ID until someone clicks Remove the pasted ID; a pasted ID turns a text value of Yes/true/1 into that ID. Choice and checkbox questions are unchanged (Map values).

entries.title: History records changes to your setup, content and scheduling
entries.summary: The **Audit** tab in event and organization **History** now records events, organization settings, portals, field rules, workflows, apps, membership, shared views, rooms, tracks, agenda publishing, forms, email campaigns, templates and system notifications, tasks, document templates, awards programs and bulk data exports. New **Type** and **Action** filters — such as **Cloned**, **Installed**, **Published**, **Scheduled** and **Export requested** — find them.

where.path: History → Audit (event and organization)

entries.use_case: When a portal, campaign schedule or app connection changes unexpectedly, the customer can see who did it and when, and hand their security team one log instead of asking support.

internal.when_to_bring_up: "Who changed this?" questions, security questionnaires about audit logging, SIEM export conversations.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer; especially enterprise and security-conscious accounts.
internal.gotchas: Only changes made after this release are recorded. Bodies, HTML, CSS and secrets show as Changed, never the value. Question-level edits on CFP, application and follow-up forms are not recorded (form settings are). Private saved views and agenda draft edits are not recorded; committing a draft is. Org-level items (org settings, apps, membership, org session forms, awards programs) are in org History, not event History.

entries.title: Send participant acceptance invitations
entries.summary: Ask participants to accept with an explicit **Send invitation**: from a session's **Acceptance invitations** section, or for many sessions at once with **Send invitations** in the Sessions bulk bar. Filter by **Not sent**, **Sent**, **Overdue** and **Blocked**, resend when needed, and see a summary of what was sent and what was skipped and why.

enable.path: Settings → Record Settings → Participant Acceptance → Enable Participant Acceptance and Save; then the Invitations and deadlines panel

where.path: Program → Sessions → session side panel or profile → Acceptance invitations; Sessions bulk bar → Send invitations

entries.use_case: Organizers finally know who has been asked and when, instead of hoping speakers notice a portal task. One email per person per session, with a record of every send.

cs_action.note: Good moment to walk acceptance customers through the new invitation flow; nothing is sent until an admin clicks Send.

internal.staff_path: Participant Acceptance itself is enabled per event (Pro tier); the invitation settings are in the same Record Settings section once it is saved on.
internal.when_to_bring_up: Customers chasing speaker confirmations by hand or by campaign; anyone asking 'did we ask them yet?'.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with Participant Acceptance on, especially large programs and medical/scientific meetings.
internal.gotchas: Sending needs the send-emails permission. Already-invited rows are skipped unless Resend is used. The bulk dialog takes up to 150 sessions. Blocked reasons are in English and may show a raw format id for format conditions.

entries.title: Accept-by deadlines for participant acceptance
entries.summary: Set **Accept-by rules** per session format and role: a fixed date or a number of days after the invitation is sent, with optional grace days. Extend a single participant's deadline from the invitations list. In the portal, participants see **Respond by** with the date, and after the deadline they are asked to contact the event team instead of changing their answer.

enable.path: Settings → Record Settings → Participant Acceptance → Enable Participant Acceptance and Save; then the Invitations and deadlines panel

where.path: Settings → Record Settings → Participant Acceptance → Invitations and deadlines → Accept-by rules; speaker portal Sessions card and Confirm dialog

entries.use_case: Programs need confirmations by a date so the agenda can lock. Deadlines per format (posters vs podium) and a clear date in the portal and emails stop the last-minute chase.

cs_action.note: Help the customer pick fixed vs rolling deadlines and grace days before they send; a past deadline locks portal answers.

internal.staff_path: Participant Acceptance itself is enabled per event (Pro tier); the invitation settings are in the same Record Settings section once it is saved on.
internal.when_to_bring_up: Any acceptance customer with a confirmation cutoff, or asking for different deadlines per format.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with Participant Acceptance on and a hard confirmation date.
internal.gotchas: A rolling rule has no date until the invitation is sent. Sessions matching no rule have no deadline. One rule per format + role. Extensions only work on sent invitations.

entries.title: Automatic reminders and overdue handling for acceptance invitations
entries.summary: Turn on **Send reminders** to email participants who have not answered at set days before **Accept by** (7 and 2 by default). When a deadline passes, the participant gets one overdue email, event admins get one notification grouped by format, and you can move them to a custom status with **When overdue, set participant status to**.

enable.path: Settings → Record Settings → Participant Acceptance → Enable Participant Acceptance and Save; then the Invitations and deadlines panel

where.path: Settings → Record Settings → Participant Acceptance → Invitations and deadlines → Send reminders

entries.use_case: Stops staff from manually chasing non-responders: reminders go out on schedule and overdue people surface in one list.

cs_action.note: Reminders are off by default; turn on Send reminders. Overdue emails and the admin notification also only run with reminders on.

internal.staff_path: Participant Acceptance itself is enabled per event (Pro tier); the invitation settings are in the same Record Settings section once it is saved on.
internal.when_to_bring_up: Customers who send weekly 'please confirm' campaigns by hand.
internal.who_should_get_it: Acceptance events with accept-by rules.
internal.gotchas: Runs hourly. Each reminder offset sends once and never on the day of the invitation. Overdue handling requires a deadline, so it does nothing without an accept-by rule.

entries.title: Choose where sub-session participants accept
entries.summary: **Ask participants to accept** sets whether a sub-session participant is asked on each session they are on (today's behavior), **on sub-sessions only**, or **on the parent and each sub-session** independently — so a panelist is no longer asked twice.

enable.path: Settings → Record Settings → Participant Acceptance → Enable Participant Acceptance and Save; then the Invitations and deadlines panel

where.path: Settings → Record Settings → Participant Acceptance → Invitations and deadlines → Ask participants to accept

entries.use_case: Debates, symposia and abstract-built sessions put people on sub-sessions; asking once at the right level avoids duplicate confirmations and confused speakers.

cs_action.note: Default stays 'On each session they are on' — no change for existing events.

internal.staff_path: Participant Acceptance itself is enabled per event (Pro tier); the invitation settings are in the same Record Settings section once it is saved on.
internal.when_to_bring_up: Customers using sub-sessions (symposia, debates, abstract sessions) who complain about double confirmations.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with sub-sessions and Participant Acceptance on.
internal.gotchas: With 'sub-sessions only', a person assigned directly to the parent with the same role as on a sub-session is treated as a rolled-up copy and is not asked on the parent.

entries.title: Hold acceptance invitations until a session is ready
entries.summary: Add **Send only when** conditions to an accept-by rule — session status, custom status, format, session date, parent session status, or another role has accepted. Participants who don't meet them show as **Blocked** with the reason and are skipped by bulk sends.

enable.path: Settings → Record Settings → Participant Acceptance → Enable Participant Acceptance and Save; then the Invitations and deadlines panel

where.path: Settings → Record Settings → Participant Acceptance → Accept-by rules → Add rule → Send only when

entries.use_case: Prevents inviting speakers to sessions that aren't accepted or scheduled yet, and lets co-presenters be invited only after the lead has confirmed.

cs_action.note: Suggest 'Session status is any of Accepted' as a safe default condition.

internal.staff_path: Participant Acceptance itself is enabled per event (Pro tier); the invitation settings are in the same Record Settings section once it is saved on.
internal.when_to_bring_up: Customers worried about inviting people too early.
internal.who_should_get_it: Acceptance events sending invitations in bulk.
internal.gotchas: Conditions apply when an admin sends; nothing sends automatically when a condition becomes true. Blocked reasons are English and may show a raw format id.

entries.title: Presenting authors of placed abstracts are asked to accept
entries.summary: When an abstract is placed into a session (for example with **Create a subsession**), its presenting author is added as a participant waiting to accept and gets the **Abstract placed into a session** email when you send the invitation. Co-authors are not invited.

enable.path: Settings → Record Settings → Participant Acceptance → Enable Participant Acceptance and Save; then the Invitations and deadlines panel

where.path: Program → Abstracts → Create a subsession; then the session's Acceptance invitations

entries.use_case: Abstract-driven meetings need every presenting author to confirm they will present in the session their abstract landed in.

cs_action.note: Only on events with Participant Acceptance on.

internal.staff_path: Participant Acceptance itself is enabled per event (Pro tier); the invitation settings are in the same Record Settings section once it is saved on.
internal.when_to_bring_up: Medical/scientific customers building sessions from abstracts.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events using Abstracts with Participant Acceptance on.
internal.gotchas: On events that use accept-by rules or a non-default level, a submitter who also presents on an accepted session stays Invited until they confirm (previously auto-confirmed). Events without rules and on the default level are unchanged.

entries.title: Accept By Date merge tag
entries.summary: Use the **Accept By Date** session merge tag (`{{accept_by_date}}`) in Send Email and Email Campaigns to show each recipient their participant acceptance deadline for the session, in the event timezone. It is empty once they have answered.

enable.path: Settings → Record Settings → Participant Acceptance → Accept-by rules; then insert Accept By Date from Merge Tags

where.path: Session merge tags in Send Email and Email Campaigns (Sessions audience)

entries.use_case: Lets organizers put the confirmation deadline in their own reminder emails without retyping dates per format.

cs_action.note: Works once the event has accept-by rules.

internal.staff_path: Participant Acceptance itself is enabled per event (Pro tier); the invitation settings are in the same Record Settings section once it is saved on.
internal.when_to_bring_up: Customers writing their own confirmation reminder campaigns.
internal.who_should_get_it: Acceptance events with accept-by rules.
internal.gotchas: Empty when acceptance is off, no rule applies, or the recipient already answered.
